findings.description: consent_records.user_agent is stored plaintext but is neither flagged by _looks_like_pii nor recorded in PLAINTEXT_EXCEPTIONS, while ip_address in the same table is an explicit reviewed exception. The consent-audit comment added in the same range ('IP and user agent stay in the consent record only, not the log stream') treats the two as equally sensitive, so the R6 policy silently covers only half of the network identifiers it claims to govern.
findings.message: consent_records.user_agent escapes the PII policy while the sibling ip_address needs a reviewed exception.
findings.fix: Add "agent" to PII_NAME_TOKENS and ('consent_records', 'user_agent') to PLAINTEXT_EXCEPTIONS with the same DPDPA-evidence rationale.

findings.description: PII_NAME_TOKENS omits the secret-shaped tokens most likely to appear next in this codebase ('token', 'otp', 'ssn', 'passport'), and 'dob' only matches as a standalone underscore token so 'date_of_birth' is missed. A future plaintext column such as telegram_bot_token, refresh_token, or date_of_birth would pass test_no_model_column_stores_pii_in_plaintext, which is the whole enforcement mechanism for R6. No such column exists today (verified by running the heuristic over every mapped column), so this is a coverage gap, not a live defect.
findings.message: PII token list misses token/otp/ssn/passport and date_of_birth, so those columns would pass the R6 gate in plaintext.
findings.fix: Add "token", "otp", "ssn", "passport", "birth" to PII_NAME_TOKENS. Do not add "key": it would false-positive on the existing master_resume.minio_key / tailored_resumes.minio_key columns.

findings.description: 172.28.0.10 is the trust anchor for the whole admin allowlist and is hardcoded in two independent places (the app's --forwarded-allow-ips at :75 and nginx's ipv4_address at :134), plus a third copy in .env.example prose. Nothing validates that they agree (CI only runs nginx -t; there is no `docker compose config` check). If the subnet or the nginx address drifts, uvicorn stops trusting nginx, every admin request is evaluated against nginx's container IP, and admin is either fully locked out or 'fixed' by adding the proxy IP to ALLOWED_IPS - the exact failure mode .env.example warns is internet-wide exposure.
findings.message: The nginx trust IP is a magic constant duplicated across two compose keys with no check that they agree.
findings.fix: Declare it once (e.g. NGINX_IP=172.28.0.10 in .env) and interpolate ${NGINX_IP:-172.28.0.10} into both the nginx ipv4_address and the app's --forwarded-allow-ips.

findings.description: APP_ENV: ${APP_ENV:-development} fails open. A compose `environment:` entry takes precedence over `env_file: .env`, so when interpolation cannot resolve APP_ENV (non-default --env-file, an explicit --project-directory, or a missing .env) the container runs as development regardless of APP_ENV=production inside the env file - re-enabling /api/docs and non-https session cookies, the precise posture R9 removed. This is on a production path: installer/core/autostart.py:49 deploys real installations with docker-compose.yml, and installer/core/env_writer.py:55 relies on APP_ENV=production being honoured. The default paths (systemd WorkingDirectory=install_dir; the Windows task's `cd /d install_dir`) do resolve correctly today, which is why this is a WARN rather than a BLOCK.
findings.message: Compose fallback ${APP_ENV:-development} can silently override a production env_file value on the installer's deployment path.
findings.fix: Use ${APP_ENV:-production}. Local dev still resolves to development because init.sh copies .env.example (APP_ENV=development) to .env, which compose interpolates.

findings.description: Docker's IPAM allocates dynamic addresses sequentially from 172.28.0.2 and does not pre-reserve statically configured addresses. With the six dynamically addressed services today the pool tops out around .7, so .10 is safe; adding three more services (or scaling one) can hand .10 to another container first, after which nginx fails to start with 'Address already in use'. nginx starts last (depends_on: app), which maximises the exposure.
findings.message: Static ipv4_address 172.28.0.10 sits inside the dynamic allocation pool.
findings.fix: Reserve the dynamic pool away from the static address: add `ip_range: 172.28.0.0/25` under the ipam config and move nginx to 172.28.0.130 (or keep .10 and set ip_range to 172.28.0.128/25).

findings.description: The same four-line guarded-router construction is repeated across all six admin routers; a seventh admin router can silently omit the dependency. The risk is contained because tests/unit/test_ip_allowlist.py:43 enumerates the app's actual routes and fails on any unguarded /api/admin path, so this is style, not exposure.
findings.message: Router-level allowlist dependency duplicated in six files.
findings.fix: Optional: pass dependencies=[Depends(require_server_ip)] once at each app.include_router(admin_*) call in app/main.py instead of in each router module.

findings.description: A denied admin request raises 403 without emitting an audit event, so an IP scan of /api/admin leaves no trace in the log stream while successful admin actions are audited. Listed as a deferred follow-up in specs/stories/CHG-002-admin-ip-allowlist.md, so it is recorded, not re-litigated.
findings.message: Denied admin attempts are not audited.
findings.fix: Call audit("admin.ip_denied", details={"client_ip": client_ip}) immediately before raising the HTTPException.

findings.description: test_unrecognised_app_env_is_rejected asserts only that some ValidationError is raised; it would pass for the wrong reason if any other required setting were missing. It is non-vacuous today because the root conftest.py seeds APP_SECRET_KEY / POSTGRES_PASSWORD / MINIO_SECRET_KEY / FERNET_KEY, but the assertion does not pin that.
findings.message: Rejection test does not assert which field failed validation.
findings.fix: Use pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="app_env") so the test can only pass for the Literal constraint.

findings.description: assert len(wired.tenant.executed) == 2 pins the number of SQL statements the handler issues rather than an observable outcome, so a behaviour-preserving refactor that merges two statements would fail it. Acceptable as deliberate characterization pinning ahead of the R15/R16 extraction work, but it should not outlive that refactor.
findings.message: Characterization test asserts internal statement count.
findings.fix: Replace with an assertion on the resulting profile state once the onboarding extraction lands.

findings.description: Assessment of the registry perf-smell BLOCK (5x PERF-N1-LOOP-QUERY at 147/169/259/277/306): false positive. get_tenant_db (app/database.py:90-96) is a single-yield async generator, so `async for tenant_db in get_tenant_db(schema)` runs exactly one iteration - it is the dependency-generator-as-context-manager idiom, not a per-row query loop. Exhausting the generator also runs its finally, so the session is closed; there is no leak. All five lines are pre-existing and untouched by this range (the diff changed only lines 94-100).
findings.message: perf-smell PERF-N1-LOOP-QUERY findings on onboarding.py are false positives on pre-existing lines.
findings.fix: No code change. Suppress or teach the perf sensor to ignore `async for x in <single-yield dependency generator>`.
